summary: August Blau was an Indologist and linguist who studied under August Friedrich Pott and Carl Cappeller, earning his Ph.D. at the University of Jena. He held library posts at Wrocław, Göttingen, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1892).

August Boeckh worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied under Friedrich August Wolf and Friedrich Schleiermacher before holding academic posts at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1811–1861).
August Clemens Schoener was an Indologist and linguist who completed theology studies at the University of Munich and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg between 1890 and 1894.

August Conrady specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. at Würzburg under Julius Jolly, studied at Strasbourg, Jena, Heidelberg, and Leipzig, and held posts at Peking University (1903–1904) and the University of Leipzig (1891–1925).
August Constantin Boltz was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena by 1845. He served as a professor at the Prussian Military Academy from 1852 to 1864.

August Dillmann worked in religious studies and linguistics. After earning a Ph.D. at Tübingen under Heinrich Ewald, Rudolf von Roth, and August Schleicher, he held professorships at Tübingen, Kiel, Giessen, and Humboldt/Frederick William University Berlin.

August Ferdinand Naeke was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Leipzig from 1805 to 1810. He held academic posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Bonn (~1818–1838).

August Fick was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, Heinrich Ewald, and Karl Friedrich Hermann. He later served as an associate professor at Göttingen (1876) and full professor at Breslau (1888–1891).

August Fischer worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1885–1889) and held posts at the University of Leipzig (~1900–1930) and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (~1903–1920).

August Friedrich Pott was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Bopp and Humboldt. After lecturing at Berlin, he served as professor of general linguistics at the University of Halle from 1833.

August Hermann Francke was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and archaeology who studied under Karl Rudolf Marx and completed his habilitation at Berlin. He served as a lecturer and extraordinary professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (1922–1930).

August Hjalmar Edgren was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held teaching posts at Yale, Lund, the University of Gothenburg, and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.

August Johan Bernet Kempers studied Indology and archaeology at Leiden under Nicolaas Johannes Krom. He served at the Kern Institute, Batavian Society, Dinas Purbakala (director 1947–1956), Netherlands Open Air Museum (1958–1970), and University of Amsterdam.

August Leskien was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He spent his career at the University of Leipzig, serving as associate professor from 1870 and professor from 1876 to 1915.
August Ludwig von Schlözer was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Uppsala University (~1755–1756) and held a post at the University of Göttingen from ~1769 to 1809.

August Schleicher was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, Erlangen, and Bonn under Ewald, Lassen, and Ritschl. He held posts at Bonn, the German University in Prague/Charles University, and Jena.
August Sundin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who is a Ph.D. student at Ghent University, attested from 2024 to 2026.

August Tholuck was a scholar of religious studies who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1816–1820). He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1821–1826) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1826–1877).
August Viktor Bergny was an Indologist and linguist who completed his fil.kand. and fil.lic. studies at Uppsala University between 1886 and 1898.

August Wilhelm von Schlegel was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Heyne, Bürger, Chézy, and Hamilton. He held an extraordinary chair at Jena (1795, 1798) and the first Indology chair at Bonn from 1818.
